title: Break-even analysis with a worked calculation for bond and end-of-lease cleaning
audience: Owners of bond and end-of-lease cleaning businesses, including solo operators, who set move-out prices or plan monthly income.
learningOutcomes: Classify the costs of a home-service business as fixed or variable
Calculate monthly break-even revenue from fixed costs and a variable cost percentage
Explain why conflicting break-even figures must be reconciled before any of them is used

instruction.heading: What break-even means for a move-out business
instruction.body: Break-even revenue is the monthly sales that cover all costs, so profit is zero. For a move-out business it shows how many move-outs must be completed before profit begins. ANZ defines fixed and variable costs and warns that costs must be covered to avoid running at a loss. A move-out business is lumpy: it depends on lease ends, so a single slow month can mislead. Use several months of figures.

instruction.heading: Split the costs for a move-out business
instruction.body: Fixed costs stay the same whatever the number of move-outs: vehicle registration and loan repayments, insurance, phone and software, and any storage. Variable costs move with each job: cleaning products, cloths, bin liners, equipment consumables and card or payment fees. Any casual cleaner paid by the hour has wages that rise with the work, so treat those wages as variable and include them in the variable share. Express variable cost as a share of sales for the same months.

instruction.heading: The formula
instruction.body: Break-even revenue equals fixed costs divided by one minus the variable share of sales. The result after variable cost is the contribution margin (Xero Australia glossary, 23 July 2026). The answer is revenue, not profit. Divide it by the average price charged per move-out, and round up to whole move-outs, because a part job does not cover costs.

instruction.heading: Work the calculation in order, and use real price inputs
instruction.body: Write each input with its period and source. Compute the contribution margin, divide the fixed costs by it, then divide by the average move-out price. The only move-out price range in the research is the Beyond Pricing band, which is a short-stay proxy. If you use its midpoint, label it as a proxy, and replace it with your own average once you have invoices.

instruction.heading: Reconcile two figures before you use either
instruction.body: When two figures disagree, check whether each fixed cost is monthly or annual, whether the variable share is of sales or of cost, and whether the output is revenue or profit. Keep only the reconciled figure, with its inputs. The research did not find bond-specific cost ratios, so every cost input must come from your own records.

procedure: List every monthly cost for the move-out business and label each one fixed or variable.
Count any casual wages as variable, along with products, bin liners and payment fees.
Work out variable cost as a share of sales for the same months, and check it across several months.
Calculate one minus the variable share, then divide monthly fixed costs by it.
Divide break-even revenue by the average price per move-out you actually charge, and round up to whole move-outs.
Compare any other figure, reconcile the inputs, and keep only the reconciled one.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A solo bond cleaner charges an average of $190 a move-out for a two-bedroom home. That is the midpoint of the Beyond Pricing two-bedroom move-out band of $160 to $220 (vendor proxy, 28 October 2026). Fixed costs are $1,800 a month and variable costs are 15 per cent of sales, both illustrative. The owner works alone.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How many move-outs must be completed each month to break even, and what should be checked before the price is used?
workedExamples.reasoning: The contribution margin is 1 - 0.15, which is 0.85. Break-even revenue is $1,800 divided by 0.85, which is $2,117.65 a month (CALC). At $190 a move-out that is 11.1, so 12 move-outs are needed. Check: 11 move-outs give $1,776.50 of contribution, short of $1,800, and 12 give $1,938.00. Each move-out contributes $161.50. Before the price is used, check that the $190 is what you actually charge, not the proxy midpoint, and that the 15 per cent includes products, bin liners and payment fees. If a casual cleaner is hired, add their wages to the variable share and run the calculation again.

equipmentAndPpe: Cost list for the last three months

commonErrors.error: Treating a casual cleaner's hours as a fixed cost.
commonErrors.prevention: Track their hours per move-out and include them in the variable share.

commonErrors.error: Using variable cost as a share of cost instead of a share of sales.
commonErrors.prevention: Divide by sales for the same months, and write the denominator beside the percentage.

commonErrors.error: Using the proxy band as the average price.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the average you actually invoice. Label any proxy and its source.

commonErrors.error: Judging break-even from one slow month of lease ends.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the variable share and the job count across several months.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business planning only. This lesson gives no tax or accounting advice. Check the tax treatment of costs with a registered tax agent or accountant. The research did not confirm the tax treatment.

The wage in any cost build is subject to the Cleaning Services Award where it applies: Level 1 adult minimum of $25.85 an hour with 25 per cent casual loading, from 1 July 2025. The 2026-27 rates were not checked.

qualityStandard: Every break-even figure shows its fixed costs, variable percentage, period and source.
Two figures that disagree are reconciled before either one is used in a plan or a price.
documentationEvidence: Cost list split into fixed and variable, with source and date
Reconciliation note wherever two figures disagree
summary: Break-even revenue is fixed costs divided by one minus the variable share of sales.
Use real invoice prices. A market band is a proxy and must be labelled as one.
Gaps: bond-specific cost ratios and move-out prices were not found in the research. Every input here is illustrative or a proxy.

knowledgeChecks.question: Break-even revenue for a move-out business is calculated as:
options: Fixed costs multiplied by the variable percentage
Fixed costs divided by (1 minus the variable share of sales)
Sales minus fixed costs, shown as a percentage of the price
Fixed costs plus variable costs for the month

knowledgeChecks.question: Fixed costs are $1,800 a month, variable costs are 15 per cent of sales, and an average move-out is $190. What is the monthly break-even revenue?
Two sources give different break-even figures for the same business. What is the right response?
options: Use the larger figure to be safe
Recalculate from your own costs, and check each source's inputs before using any figure
Average the two figures and quote the result
Skip the check and rely on the owner's gut feel

sourceReferences: ANZ, 'Setting the right price for your product or service', https://www.anz.com.au/business/business-hub/starting-business/start/setting-the-right-price-for-your-product-or-service/, dated 21 February 2025, last modified 22 July 2025. Supports: definitions of fixed and variable costs; costs must be covered to avoid running at a loss.

Xero Australia, 'Break-even point formula' glossary entry, https://www.xero.com/au/glossary/break-even-point-formula/, dated 23 July 2026. Supports: contribution margin is price minus variable cost; break-even revenue is fixed costs divided by the contribution ratio; job counts are rounded up to whole jobs.

Beyond Pricing, 'Short-term rental cleaning fees (Australia)', https://beyondpricing.com/au/blog/how-much-should-you-charge-for-cleaning-fees-in-your-australian-holiday-rental, dated 28 October 2026. Vendor source; short-stay fee data. Supports: per-turnover bands by property size; move-in and move-out bands by bedroom count; a $120 per-turnover illustration; city labour benchmarks; fixed rates suit smaller properties and hourly rates suit larger or luxury homes.

Fair Work Commission, Cleaning Services Award (MA000022), https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000022.html, variation effective 1 July 2025. Supports: Level 1 adult minimum hourly rate of $25.85 and a 25 per cent casual loading. The 1 July 2026 position was not checked.

Notes: the $1,800 fixed costs, 15 per cent variable share and two-bedroom move-out are illustrative. The $190 is the midpoint of a vendor proxy band, labelled as such. CALC marks arithmetic on those inputs.
